result.scientific_strategy:
## abd93958-a0b2-4d26-b212-96ebeb401d22 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the unchanged official two-joint-arm task. The fresh PPO baseline in experiment 1 reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.0% on the protected task-reference panel at checkpoint-100352, while its endpoint regressed on both panels. Experiment 2 transferred that checkpoint and expanded training coverage to the official 6-20 cm radius range; its selected checkpoint reached 97.0% on the researcher panel and 98.5% on the task-reference panel. Experiment 3 transferred the same lineage and added joint-configuration progress shaping, but its measured mid-run checkpoints matched experiment 2 and retained the same task-reference failures, while its endpoint regressed to 96.5%/97.0%. Experiment 4 oversampled the previously observed negative-angle regions, but its mid-run and endpoint candidates remained below the unchanged working policy on both comparable controls; the endpoint reached 97.0% on the task-reference panel versus 98.5% for working. The campaign therefore has a near-objective policy with no robust cross-panel attainment; experiment 2 checkpoint-100352 remains the strongest measured development policy. This is provisional memory for reassessment and does not prescribe a next action.

**Lessons and limits:** Measured task success, rather than logged reward or training success, is the policy-progress signal. All four experiments identify checkpoint selection or recipe effects as important: proxy metrics did not reliably predict measured task success. Experiment 2 reduced the task-reference failures from four to three, recovering two short-radius negative-angle cases, but left failures at 9.4-9.9 cm and about -123 to -128 degrees plus one 18.2 cm case at -154.8 degrees. Experiment 3's 80,896- and 100,352-step candidates preserved exactly those three task-reference failures and the same six researcher-panel failures; the 120,832-step endpoint added three further task-reference failures. In experiment 4, the focused curriculum's mid-run candidate failed 11 task-reference episodes and its endpoint failed six, while working failed only the same three persistent cases. The task-reference candidates also introduced new failures outside the focused regions. The sampler intervention therefore did not resolve the targeted cases or preserve broad measured behavior under this transferred recipe, although this comparison does not isolate target frequency from transfer or PPO optimization dynamics. The observation representation includes errors to both valid inverse-kinematics branches, while the reward directly shapes Cartesian progress and hold completion. Fixed 200-episode panels remain development evidence and are not the official 200-episode assessment.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether the residual failures reflect underrepresented target regions, PPO optimization dynamics, a limitation of the transferred policy, or ordinary fresh-training variance. The experiment-4 result weakens, but does not disprove, insufficient target exposure as an explanation because it tested one transferred sampler and training trajectory. It is also unknown whether the full-radius recipe reproduces its experiment-2 behavior from fresh initialization, whether a policy that improves the residual regions preserves broad success, and whether any development-panel gain generalizes to the official final assessment.
